chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, the seller of garments, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the believer commits a sin, then he is reminded of it after twenty years, so he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it, and He forgives him; and He reminds him only so that He may forgive him. And indeed, the disbeliever commits a sin, so he forgets it from the moment he commits it.
ai.seo_question: How does Allah's reminder of sin differ between a believer and a disbeliever?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the divine mercy inherent in the believer's spiritual journey, where Allah intentionally delays the reminder of a sin for up to twenty years to provide ample opportunity for sincere repentance (tawbah). In contrast, the disbeliever's immediate forgetting signifies a state of heedlessness (ghaflah) that prevents the recognition of sin and the subsequent seeking of pardon. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that forgetting for the disbeliever is a form of punishment, whereas delayed reminder for the believer is a mercy.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba Baya’a Al Aksiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Momin commits the sin, then he remembers after twenty years, so he seeks Forgiveness of Allahazwj from it, and Heazwj Forgives him, and rather Heazwj Reminds him in order to Forgive him for it; and that the Kafir (unbeliever) commits the sin, so he forgets it from its time (of committing it)’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah Bayya’ al-Aksiyah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

A believer commits a sin and remembers it after twenty years, then he pleads before Allah for forgiveness, He still forgives him. He is made to remember so He may forgive him. An unbeliever commits a sin and forgets it within the same hour.’”
